group: No discriminator – single valid schema (happy path)

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=true, discriminator disabled, reportChildErrors=false, canShortCircuit=true

cases.expected: empty Set – no ValidationMessage (numberOfValidSchema == 1, errors == null)
cases.description: Discriminator keyword is disabled, only one schema is supplied and its validate() returns an empty set, so the OneOfValidator should report success.

group: No discriminator – multiple valid schemas, short‑circuit enabled

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=false, discriminator disabled, reportChildErrors=false, canShortCircuit=true

cases.expected: Set containing one ValidationMessage with messageKey "oneOf.indexes" and arguments "2, 0, 1" (two valid schemas, short‑circuit after the second).
cases.description: Two schemas validate successfully. canShortCircuit() returns true, so the loop breaks after the second valid schema. The validator must return a OneOf error reporting the indexes of the two matching schemas.

group: No discriminator – multiple valid schemas, short‑circuit disabled

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=false, discriminator disabled, reportChildErrors=false, canShortCircuit=false
valid JsonNode matching all three schemas

cases.expected: Set containing one ValidationMessage with messageKey "oneOf.indexes" and arguments "3, 0, 1, 2" (all three schemas are valid).
cases.description: Three schemas are valid, canShortCircuit() returns false, therefore the loop iterates over all schemas and the validator reports a OneOf error listing all three matching indexes.

group: No discriminator – no schema matches

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=true, discriminator disabled, reportChildErrors=true, canShortCircuit=true

cases.expected: Set containing one ValidationMessage with messageKey "oneOf" and argument "0" (zero valid schemas). Child errors from each schema are also present in the returned set.
cases.description: All schemas return non‑empty error sets. reportChildErrors() is true, so child errors are collected. Since numberOfValidSchema == 0, a OneOf error with count 0 is produced together with the child errors.

group: Discriminator enabled – matching discriminator property

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=false, discriminator enabled, canShortCircuit=true, reportChildErrors=false, DiscriminatorContext active

cases.expected: empty Set – validation succeeds (discriminator matches $ref of the only valid schema, numberOfValidSchema == 1, no errors).
cases.description: Discriminator keyword is enabled. The parent schema contains a discriminator validator with propertyName "type" and mapping {"A":"#/components/schemas/A"}. The node contains "type":"A" which matches the $ref of the first schema, causing the discriminator context to mark a match. Because a match is found, no discriminator‑related error is emitted and the OneOf rule is satisfied.

group: Discriminator enabled – discriminator present but no matching $ref

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=false, discriminator enabled, canShortCircuit=true, reportChildErrors=false, DiscriminatorContext active

cases.expected: Set containing one ValidationMessage with messageKey "oneOf" and argument "0" AND a discriminator‑specific message: "based on the provided discriminator. No alternative could be chosen based on the discriminator property".
cases.description: Discriminator is enabled, the node contains the discriminator property but its value does not correspond to any $ref in the candidate schemas. The discriminator context does not mark a match, so after the loop the validator adds the special discriminator error and then the generic OneOf error (since numberOfValidSchema == 0).

group: Discriminator enabled – discriminator property missing (ignore path)

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=false, discriminator enabled, canShortCircuit=true, reportChildErrors=false, DiscriminatorContext active

cases.expected: Set containing one ValidationMessage with messageKey "oneOf" and argument "0" (no valid schemas). No discriminator‑specific error because the context is marked as ignore.
cases.description: The discriminator property is absent; the discriminator context marks IGNORE. Consequently the validator does not emit the special discriminator‑no‑match message. Since no schemas validate, a normal OneOf error with count 0 is returned.

group: Walk flag true – schema validation via walk()

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=false, discriminator disabled, reportChildErrors=false, canShortCircuit=true
valid JsonNode that passes walk() of first schema only

cases.expected: empty Set – one schema validates via walk(), numberOfValidSchema == 1, no errors.
cases.description: When the walk flag is true the validator calls schema.walk() instead of schema.validate(). The mock schema returns an empty set, leading to a successful OneOf validation.

group: Discriminator disabled – child errors collected when reportChildErrors true

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=false, discriminator disabled, reportChildErrors=true, canShortCircuit=false

cases.expected: Set containing one ValidationMessage with messageKey "oneOf" (count 0) and also the child ValidationMessages from both schemas (unioned).
cases.description: Discriminator is off, but reportChildErrors() returns true, so the validator must collect the error sets from each failing schema and include them together with the final OneOf error.

group: FailFast flag propagation – error message includes failFast true

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=true, discriminator disabled, reportChildErrors=true, canShortCircuit=false
invalid JsonNode that fails both schemas (e.g., {"a":"string"})

cases.expected: Set containing a ValidationMessage with messageKey "oneOf" whose failFast flag is true, plus the child ValidationMessages from both schemas.
cases.description: When ExecutionContext.failFast is true the generated OneOf ValidationMessage must carry failFast=true. The test verifies that the flag is propagated correctly.

group: FailFast flag propagation – error message includes failFast false

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=false, discriminator disabled, reportChildErrors=true, canShortCircuit=false
invalid JsonNode that fails both schemas

cases.expected: Set containing a ValidationMessage with messageKey "oneOf" whose failFast flag is false, plus the child ValidationMessages from both schemas.
cases.description: When ExecutionContext.failFast is false the OneOf ValidationMessage must have failFast=false. This mirrors the previous test but with the flag cleared.

group: Discriminator enabled but no discriminator validator present – behaves like normal OneOf

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=false, discriminator enabled, canShortCircuit=false, reportChildErrors=false, DiscriminatorContext active

cases.expected: Set containing one ValidationMessage with messageKey "oneOf" and argument "0" (no schemas match). No discriminator‑specific message is produced because no discriminator validator exists in the parent schema.
cases.description: Even though the configuration enables discriminators, if the parent schema does not contain a discriminator validator the validator should fall back to the normal OneOf logic.

group: Discriminator enabled – match found but another schema also validates (indexes reported)

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=false, discriminator enabled, canShortCircuit=false, reportChildErrors=false, DiscriminatorContext active
JsonNode {"type":"A", "extra":1} (matches discriminator and also satisfies second schema)

cases.expected: Set containing one ValidationMessage with messageKey "oneOf.indexes" and arguments "2, 0, 1" (both schemas are valid). No discriminator‑specific error is emitted because a match was found.
cases.description: When a discriminator matches a schema but other schemas also validate, the validator must still report the generic OneOf error with all matching indexes. The discriminator does not suppress the generic error when more than one schema is valid.

group: Walk flag true with discriminator enabled – matching discriminator leads to success

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=false, discriminator enabled, canShortCircuit=true, reportChildErrors=false, DiscriminatorContext active

cases.expected: empty Set – the schema selected by the discriminator validates successfully via walk(), so numberOfValidSchema == 1 and no errors are returned.
cases.description: Ensures that when walk=true the validator calls schema.walk() even when discriminators are active, and a matching discriminator still results in a successful OneOf validation.

group: ReportChildErrors false – child errors are not included in result

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=false, discriminator disabled, reportChildErrors=false, canShortCircuit=false
invalid JsonNode that fails both schemas

cases.expected: Set containing only one ValidationMessage with messageKey "oneOf" (argument "0"). No child ValidationMessages from the individual schemas are present.
cases.description: When reportChildErrors() returns false the validator must not union the individual schema error sets into the final result, even though all schemas failed.

group: Single valid schema with child errors present – child errors ignored

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=false, discriminator disabled, reportChildErrors=true, canShortCircuit=false
JsonNode that validates against the second schema but fails the first (e.g., {"b":2})

cases.expected: empty Set – because exactly one schema validates, the OneOf validator returns success and discards the child errors collected from the failing schema.
cases.description: Even though reportChildErrors is true and a failing schema produced errors, when exactly one schema is valid the validator must return an empty set, ignoring the previously collected child errors.

group: Short‑circuit true – first two schemas valid, third not evaluated

input.value: mock ExecutionContext with failFast=false, discriminator disabled, reportChildErrors=false, canShortCircuit=true
JsonNode that matches schema0 and schema1 but not schema2 (e.g., {"a":1, "b":2})

cases.expected: Set containing one ValidationMessage with messageKey "oneOf.indexes" and arguments "2, 0, 1". The third schema is never evaluated because short‑circuit stops after the second valid schema.
cases.description: Verifies that canShortCircuit() stops the loop as soon as more than one valid schema is found, even when additional schemas exist.

group: Null executionContext – NPE

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: The method dereferences executionContext (e.g., executionContext.isFailFast()) before any null‑check, so passing a null ExecutionContext must raise NPE.

group: Null node – NPE

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: The code accesses node (e.g., node.get(...)) without a null guard; a null node should cause NPE.

group: Null parent schema – NPE

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: When the parent schema is null, the call this.getParentSchema().getValidators() triggers NPE. Mock the OneOfValidator subclass to return null from getParentSchema().

group: Parent schema without validators – NPE

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: If the parent schema exists but its getValidators() returns null, the subsequent stream operation causes NPE. Mock parent schema to return null validators.

group: Discriminator validator of wrong type – ClassCastException

cases.expected: ClassCastException
cases.description: The code assumes the first validator with keyword "discriminator" is a DiscriminatorValidator and casts it directly. Provide a parent schema whose validator list contains a mock validator with keyword "discriminator" but of a different class; the cast should fail.

group: Discriminator schema node not ObjectNode – ClassCastException

cases.expected: ClassCastException
cases.description: When discriminator is present the code casts discriminator.getSchemaNode() to ObjectNode. Mock a DiscriminatorValidator whose schemaNode is a JsonNode of type ArrayNode (or any non‑ObjectNode). The cast should throw ClassCastException.
